out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. PIC WAS UNABLE TO PROVIDE CLEAN-UP PROCEDURES DURING INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: PROCEDURES EMAILED TO PIC. ENSURE THESE ARE KEPT ONSITE AT ALL TIMES.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: OBSERVED NO PAPER TOWEL AT THE HANDWASHING SINK IN THE WOMENS RESTROOM.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. ENSURE WOMENS RESTROOM IS PROVIDED WITH A HAND DRYING PROVISION BY JULY 27TH.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: OBSERVED PIC USING HANDWASHING SINK IN THE KITCHEN FOR DUMPING AND FILLING SANITIZER SOLUTION AND RINSING THERMOMETER.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED ON HANDWASHING SINK USEAGE.

out_items.name: Food obtained from approved source

violations.title: Molluscan Shellfish, Source on ISSC List
violations.observation: Molluscan shellfish (oysters, clams, mussels) offered for sale or service are not received from sources that are listed in the Interstate Certified Shellfish Shippers List. OBSERVED CLAMS WITH NO IDENTIFICATION/TAGS REMOVED BEING OFFERED FOR SERVICE.
violations.corrective_action: Molluscan shellfish received in interstate commerce shall be from sources that are listed in the Interstate Certified Shellfish Shippers List. CDI: PIC INFORMED TO NOT SELL/OFFER FOR SALE SHELLFISH WITHOUT ENSURING THEY ARE FROM AN APPROVED SOURCE ON THE ISSC LIST.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock, Retaining Labels/Tags for 90 Days
violations.observation: The tags for the molluscan shellfish are not being retained for 90 days. OBSERVED FACILITY NOT KEEPING ANY TAGS FOR RAW SHELLFISH.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels for 90 calendar days from the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served using one of the following methods: 1) an approved record keeping system that keeps the tags or labels in chronological order correlated to the date when the last shellstock from a container are sold or served, 2) preserving source identification by using a record keeping system, and 3) ensuring that shellstock from one tagged or labeled container are not commingled with shellstock from another container with different certification numbers, different harvest dates, or different growing areas as identified on the tag or label before being ordered by the consumer. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED ON SHELLFISH TAGS. YOU MUST KEEP SHELLFISH TAGS AS DETAILED ABOVE. BELLISSIMO RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 07/17/2026) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED IN TWO-DOOR STANDING: RAW VEAL STORED OVER COOKED MEAT SAUCE. OBSERVED IN THREE-DOOR UNDER COUNTER: RAW TENDERLOIN STORED OVER HEAVY CREAM.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: RAW ANIMAL FOODS MOVED BELOW RTE FOODS. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. OBSERVED IN TWO-DOOR STANDING: COOKED MEAT SAUCE AT 45F (COOKED THE NIGHT PRIOR), COOKED MARINARA AT 46F (COOKED THE NIGHT PRIOR).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. CDI: FOODS LISTED ABOVE DISPOSED OF.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED THREE CONTAINERS OF BREADING/FLOUR USED FOR BREADING RAW ANIMAL FOODS LEFT ON THE COUNTER FOR >1 DAY. AMBIENT AIR TEMPERATURE WAS 83F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: BREADING DISPOSED OF.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED NO DATE MARKING IN FACILITY AND PIC CONFIRMED THAT TCS FOODS ARE HELD >24HRS. ITEMS INCLUDED: COOKED PASTA, MARINARA, MEAT SAUCES, CUT TOMATOES, CUT LEAFY GREENS
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC RE-EDUCATED ON DATE MARKING. ENSURE ALL TCS FOODS HELD ONSITE FOR >24HRS ARE MARKED AS INDICATED ABOVE. CORRECT BY JULY 27TH.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED MARINARA AND MEAT SAUCE COOKED THE NIGHT BEFORE TO BE TIGHTLY COVERED.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED. FOODS DISPOSED OF DUE TO COOLING VIOLATION.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: OBSERVED OILS AND SAUCES WITHOUT LABELS.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. ENSURE ALL SQUEEZE BOTTLES AND OTHER WORKING CONTAINERS OF FOOD ARE LABELED WITH THEIR COMMON NAME BY YOUR NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers were observed reused for the storage of TCS FOODS.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. REPLACE ALL RE-USED MANUFACTURER CONTAINERS WITH NSF APPROVED CONTAINERS OR THE EQUIVALENT BY YOUR NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: OBSERVED SMALL NON-NSF TOTES BEING USED TO STORE FOOD. TOTES WERE CRACKED AND BROKEN
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. BROKEN TOTES DISPOSED OF DURING INSPECTION. ALL NON NSF TOTES MUST BE REPLACED WITH NSF APPROVED CONTAINERS OR THE EQUIVALENT BY YOUR NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: breading stations on the counter did not have time marking for using time as a public health control
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. PIC marked breading stations with start and end times

violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: display signs for the consumer advisory for the veal and steak were not on display
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed common use utensils on the Cookline being stored in on heated standing water
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC disposed of water and agreed to switch to dry storage of utensils
